contradicting_evidence: BTC has resisted the larger losses seen in ETH and many altcoins, leaving stabilization or rebound possible.
Positive displayed depth and the small positive settled ETH ETF flow argue against assuming uniform withdrawal of support.
A single weak breadth snapshot and one hourly derivatives observation cannot establish a persistent three-day trend.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: Renewed weakness following intermittent stabilization is modestly favored. BTC could remain comparatively firm while ETH and mid/small-alt proxies struggle, limiting broad recovery. A durable upward reversal would require participation and relative-strength improvement not yet demonstrated.
falsification_conditions: Repeated observations show advancing participation broadening across large, mid and small-alt proxies alongside sustained BTC and ETH recovery.
ETH/BTC strengthens persistently and newly settled flow observations improve, rather than a rebound occurring only in BTC.
Current weakness fails to persist while spot demand absorbs selling without continued leveraged expansion.
missing_evidence: Subsequent settled ETF sessions are needed to test whether the October 23 flow pattern persists.
Repeated capitalization-bucket readings are needed to distinguish sustained transmission weakness from a temporary cross-sectional pattern.
No confirmed stablecoin deployment or sufficiently long spot/derivatives sequence establishes the next three-day demand balance.
supporting_evidence: Large-, mid- and small-alt proxy advance ratios are approximately 33%, 23% and 29%; all three proxy median returns are negative.
The mid- and small-alt proxy equal-weight returns are -1.64% and -1.39%, versus BTC at -0.21%, showing limited participation beyond BTC resilience.
The latest final BTC ETF session recorded $137.9 million of outflows; ETH's $4.4 million inflow is counterevidence, not broad synchronized demand.
Stablecoin supply declined approximately 0.15% over one day, 0.68% over seven days and 0.54% over 30 days, with deployment unconfirmed.
The 30d altseason score is 22, with only 11 of 49 constituents outperforming BTC, reinforcing weak recent alt-relative participation without fixing the prospective outcome.
